disposition_reason: The primary is the complete FAO/WHO 2023 publication of CXC 81-2022 (20 PDF pages, ISBN 978-92-5-137812-0, DOI 10.4060/cc5333en). It is a non-binding code of practice listing pre-planting, production-to-harvest, post-harvest and transport practices to prevent and reduce Cd in cocoa beans; it contains no occurrence data, no maximum levels and no measured effect sizes, so every practice is extracted as guidance.

study.material_scope: cocoa beans (seed of Theobroma cacao) from planting through fermentation, drying, storage and transport
study.method: not applicable (soil analysis advice only: accredited labs, validated methods, CRMs)

controls.control: Before planting a new plantation, carry out physical-chemical soil analysis that is not limited to Cd: % organic matter, CEC, soluble Zn, chlorinity; physical (sand, clay, silt %, texture class) and, where appropriate, chemical parameters (pH, OM %, total N %, available P, K, Pb, Fe oxides/hydroxides, Mn carbonates, Cd, Zn; exchangeable Ca, Mg, K, Na, Al, H; CEC; base and Al saturation). Consult a qualified professional to interpret.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: National or relevant food control authorities should consider source-directed measures under CXC 49-2001.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only
controls.locator: Section 4.1.1, printed p.3 and note 1 (PDF p.9, p.14)

controls.control: In new plantations consider cover crops of perennial legumes (improve soil organic matter, protect against erosion and nutrient loss, reduce metal bioavailability).
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: No specific recommendation on soil Cd levels for cocoa-growing areas has been identified; acceptable soil Cd depends on soil acidity.
controls.outcome: No numeric soil Cd criterion given (statement of absence).

controls.control: Monitor irrigation water as a potential Cd source (e.g. above background from point-source contamination); as one possible guideline for higher levels, the WHO drinking-water Cd value of 0.005 mg/L is cited.
controls.outcome: Reference value cited: 0.005 mg/L Cd (WHO drinking water), offered only as one possible guideline for irrigation water.

controls.control: Agroforestry versus monoculture: data are preliminary; studies that systematically compared them found no statistically significant difference in Cd uptake in cocoa beans. Shade-species guidance (Musaceae temporary shade; Erythrina, Inga permanent; timber and fruit trees; short shade trees, citrus/fruit trees at borders).
controls.outcome: Reported as no statistically significant difference in bean Cd uptake; no numbers given.

controls.control: Site plantations, if possible, away from roads (or reduce exposure to combustion-engine emissions) and away from city dumpsites, mining, smelting, industrial wastes, sewage and household wastewater.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Avoid flooded soils if the water sources are contaminated with Cd.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Long-term: when planting new plantations, plant cocoa varieties less prone to Cd uptake.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Analyse any organic or inorganic amendment for Cd before applying it to the crop; sewage sludge, fly ashes and phosphate fertilizers can have high Cd.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Phosphate fertilizers for cocoa farms should contain low Cd and meet national criteria for the Cd:P or Cd:P2O5 ratio; phosphate fertilizers or sedimentary phosphate rock only where demonstrated low Cd and compliant with national/regional limits; verify heavy-metal content of NPK fertilizers by analysis before application; supply P preferably through organic fertilizers (high P bioavailability, low Cd).
controls.outcome: No numeric ratio given; defers to national criteria.
controls.locator: Sections 4.2.1 and 4.2.2, printed pp.4 and 6 (PDF pp.10, 12)

controls.control: Soil characterization by accredited laboratories using validated methods with certified reference materials, standards and stated uncertainties; internationally recognized methods, including ones usable by exporting farmers; include nutrients not only Cd. Soil pH is the most important parameter to measure on an ongoing basis.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Soil sampling protocol: samples representative of each farm; at least one composite sample of at least 20 subsamples per hectare; depth 0-15 cm (litterfall can enrich the top 0-5 cm, so 0-15 cm is more representative); follow international standards for metal-contaminated soils.
controls.outcome: Protocol numbers: >=1 composite of >=20 subsamples per ha; 0-15 cm depth.

controls.control: Where bean Cd is of concern and soil is alkaline (pH > 7.0), determine soil and irrigation-water salinity/electrical conductivity; EC should be less than 2 mS/cm (chloride increases Cd uptake).
controls.outcome: Target value: EC < 2 mS/cm for soil and water in alkaline soils.

controls.control: Where soil Zn is deficient, increase soil Zn (Cd competes with Zn for uptake); apply zinc sulphate with annual fertilization according to crop need and soil Zn; high rates used to inhibit Cd uptake on high-Cd soils (e.g. 25 kg Zn/ha) can acidify soil and require limestone. Authorities may set critical soil Zn levels.
controls.outcome: Example rate cited: 25 kg Zn/ha (caution about acidification); no Cd outcome given.

controls.control: Liming when soil pH is below 6 is described as the most effective method developed to date to decrease Cd bioavailability; manage soil to pH > 6 (higher may be needed where soil Cd is high) without reducing micronutrient availability; verify lime does not contain Cd; maintain Zn via ZnSO4 if needed.
controls.outcome: Targets: soil pH > 6; no measured bean-Cd effect size given.

controls.control: Apply lime in low doses (3 t/ha/year), preferably as dolomite CaMg(CO3)2, to raise pH gradually; avoid over-liming.
controls.outcome: Dose: 3 t/ha/year; no measured Cd outcome given.

controls.control: Increase soil organic matter (treated manure from stabled livestock, compost); field studies suggest more organic matter may increase Cd adsorption and help decrease bean Cd.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Apply soil amendments chosen for the soil (magnesium, sulphate, dolomitic limestone, vinasse, zeolite, humus, charcoal, calcium sulphate, cane by-products/bagasse, zinc sulphate); these can help decrease bean Cd.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Vinasse: a K source promoting mycorrhizal fungi in cocoa roots, increasing P-nutrition efficiency and immobilizing Cd.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Lime and sugar cane cake can reduce soil Cd bioavailability; zeolite is an option in sandy and clay-textured soils; avoid apatite (rock phosphate), which can contain Cd, where possible.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Biochar: shown to reduce Cd uptake into cocoa beans, with reductions comparable to liming and possibly additive to liming; biochar and compost affect soil properties, metal bioavailability and enzyme activity.
controls.outcome: Stated as comparable to liming; no numbers given.

controls.control: Grafting onto rootstocks of genotypes with low Cd bioaccumulation, and breeding new varieties less prone to Cd uptake; tried only experimentally, a longer-term measure.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only
controls.locator: Section 1 (printed p.1, PDF p.7) and Section 4.2.2 (printed pp.6-7, PDF pp.12-13)

controls.control: Remove pruned cocoa and shade-tree limbs and leaves from the ground (litter can release Cd into topsoil), particularly in orchards with high foliar Cd.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Avoid the application of sewage sludge.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Avoid burial or incineration of household waste.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: National or regional authorities should consider limiting main polluting industries near cocoa plantations (non-ferrous mining and smelting, metal-using industries, leather tanning, coal combustion, phosphate fertilizer manufacturing).
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Mucilage draining during fermentation: studies have shown draining times up to 12, 24 or 36 hours reduce Cd concentrations without affecting organoleptic quality.
controls.outcome: Direction only (reduction); no magnitudes given.

controls.control: Protect fermenting beans from smoke, dryer or vehicle gases and industrial discharges.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Increasing Saccharomyces cerevisiae concentration during fermentation can help reduce bean Cd (experimental studies; yeast absorbs Cd).
controls.outcome: Direction only; experimental; no magnitudes given.

controls.control: After fermentation, dry beans on clean solid surfaces to avoid soil contamination (drying defined as reducing moisture to below 8%).
controls.outcome: Moisture target < 8% is from the Definitions (Section 3), not a Cd outcome.
controls.locator: Section 4.3 printed p.7 (PDF p.13); Section 3 printed p.2 (PDF p.8)

controls.control: During storage prevent contamination from fuel spills, exhaust gases or fumes.
controls.outcome: no measured outcome given; recommendation only

controls.control: Transport phase: Cover loading/unloading areas to protect from rain.
controls.outcome: Good transport practice; the CoP gives no Cd-specific rationale or outcome.

controls.control: Transport phase: Ensure vehicles are well maintained and thoroughly cleaned.
controls.outcome: Good transport practice; the CoP gives no Cd-specific rationale or outcome.

controls.control: Transport phase: Ensure tarpaulins/covers are clean and undamaged.
controls.outcome: Good transport practice; the CoP gives no Cd-specific rationale or outcome.

controls.control: Transport phase: Ensure containers have not been used for chemicals or noxious substances and are maintained and clean.
controls.outcome: Good transport practice; the CoP gives no Cd-specific rationale or outcome.

controls.control: Transport phase: Keep humidity as low as possible (ventilated containers if available; cardboard/kraft paper lining).
controls.outcome: Good transport practice; the CoP gives no Cd-specific rationale or outcome.

controls.control: Transport phase: Bagged cocoa: load carefully and cover with condensation-absorbing materials.
controls.outcome: Good transport practice; the CoP gives no Cd-specific rationale or outcome.

controls.control: Transport phase: Bulk cocoa: use a sealable plastic liner if possible, kept clear of the container roof.
controls.outcome: Good transport practice; the CoP gives no Cd-specific rationale or outcome.

controls.control: Transport phase: Keep container ventilation holes free from clogging.
controls.outcome: Good transport practice; the CoP gives no Cd-specific rationale or outcome.

controls.control: Transport phase: To the extent feasible avoid temperature fluctuations and storage near noxious materials.
controls.outcome: Good transport practice; the CoP gives no Cd-specific rationale or outcome.

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary says raw_path null and SHA-256 pending; the full FAO PDF now exists at the AUDIT source-gap-resolution path (sha256 a2e30fc6...7aff), retrieved from https://www.fao.org/4/cc5333en/cc5333en.pdf per retrieval-round1.json.
Stored summary calls CXC 81-2022 the first commodity-specific Codex Cd CoP and says CCCF17 extends it to rice, cereals, fish etc.; neither statement appears in the primary.
Stored summary links the CXC 49-2001 source-directed-measures reference to sources/codex-cccf17-2024; the primary cites CXC 49-2001 (FAO/WHO 2001), a different document.
Stored summary describes the pre-planting soil parameters as 'required'; the primary says chemical analysis 'should consider where appropriate' these parameters.
Stored summary says mucilage draining 'for 12, 24, or 36 hours'; the primary says draining times 'up to 12, 24 or 36 hours' reduce Cd and gives no magnitudes.

Stored summary omits two primary statements: no specific recommendation on soil Cd levels for cocoa-growing areas has been identified (4.1.1), and systematic comparisons found no statistically significant difference in bean Cd uptake between agroforestry and monoculture (4.1.1).
Stored summary places the <8% moisture target under post-harvest practice; in the primary it is part of the Definitions (Drying), not a 4.3 recommendation.
